title: fix(lint): flow-update-readonly-field on an autolaunched flow names the elevated flow a button can start
body:
Part of #32666

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: follow-up #32832

The skill's line 158 ("Writing a `readonly` field? Set `runAs: 'system'`") gives the same remedy without the limit this PR adds to the lint fix line. `skills/**` is not this PR's to edit.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:`flow-update-readonly-field` 在 `autolaunched` 流程上的修复提示,不再只说「声明 `runAs:'system'`」,而是写明按钮能启动的提权流程只有 `screen` / `api` 流程或经 `subflow` 节点调用;`os explain` 同步写明这一限制。另在发布门加了两道写入门的回归钉子。
- 为什么改:卡上的「提交审批」按钮按原提示改成 `runAs:'system'` 后会被启动准入规则 403 拒绝,提示把人引向一条走不通的路;实测证伪了卡的机理——流程保存与 `publish-drafts` 两道门都会拒收该流程,卡上现象只在「流程先上线、对象后改只读」的反向顺序下复现,这一半是契约/产品分叉,留待席位裁决。
- 风险与回滚:只改 lint 的提示文本与说明文字,规则、严重级别与拒收范围不变;新增测试只钉住现有行为。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/lint/src/validate-readonly-flow-writes.ts` 的 hint 三元分支;`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-publish-drafts-closure.test.ts` 末尾的 `[#32666]` describe;`packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts` 新增的一段。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/validate-readonly-flow-writes.test.ts`,预期 56 个用例全绿,其中 `[#32666]` 一组看到 `'screen' or 'api' flow` 与 `subflow node`。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地;反向顺序那一半(对象改只读时是否复判已上线流程)由席位裁决后另行派发。

## What changes

- **The fix line of `flow-update-readonly-field` on an `autolaunched` flow** (`packages/lint/src/validate-readonly-flow-writes.ts`). The remedy used to be `runAs:'system'` alone. On an `autolaunched` flow, the type a record action button starts, that remedy breaks the button: `flowStartRefusal` (`packages/runtime/src/flow-start-admission.ts`) refuses a non-system caller an elevated `autolaunched`, `record_change` or `schedule` flow with 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` at every door that starts a flow by name. The line now names what a button can start:
  - `update_record`: `Declare the flow runAs:'system' (a button starts an elevated flow only as a 'screen' or 'api' flow, or through a subflow node), or remove 'FIELD' from this update_record node`
  - `create_record`: `Stamp 'FIELD' in a beforeInsert hook on 'OBJECT', or remove it from this create_record node; runAs:'system' from a button needs a 'screen' or 'api' flow or a subflow node`
  - `record_change`, `schedule`, `screen` and `api` flows keep the line they had: the first two start on their own trigger, where elevation is admitted, and the last two are entries a button can start elevated.
- **`os explain flow-update-readonly-field`** (`packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`) gains one paragraph: the limit, the refusal's code, and both routes a button can reach (a `screen` or `api` flow declared `runAs: 'system'`, which admits whoever holds its `requiredPermissions`; or a user-run flow whose `subflow` node calls the elevated flow, which then writes as the system, pinned in service-automation's `crud-runas.test.ts`).
- **Door pins** (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-publish-drafts-closure.test.ts`, one top-level `describe` in the file that already pins a flow judged against the batch closure): the card's flow is refused by `publish-drafts` with its object in the same batch and in a later batch, and by the live save door with `422 INVALID_METADATA`. The control publishes the remedy the new fix line names, a `screen` flow declared `runAs: 'system'`.
- A `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/lint`.

## Why

The card's mechanism, measured before any code (the dispatch's assumption was that the per-write flow snapshot carries no object definitions):

| Door and order | Stub harness (real `publishPackageDrafts` / `saveMetaItem`) | Real showcase kernel (REST, `bootShowcase`) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `publish-drafts`, object and flow drafted in one batch | refused, `flow-update-readonly-field` | refused, `flow-update-readonly-field` (batch rolled back) |
| object published first, flow published in a later batch | refused | refused |
| live save of the flow (`PUT /meta/flow/NAME?package=PKG`), object live | refused 422 | refused 422 |
| flow published while `status` is writable, then the object republished with `readonly: true` | object publishes clean | object publishes clean (`outcome: published`, no finding); `POST /automation/FLOW/trigger` answers `success: true`, `acted: 1`, `failed: 0`; the server logs the drop WARN |

So the assumption is falsified: on a FLOW write, both doors hand the rule the object universe (registry, stored rows and the batch's own drafts) and it refuses. The card's exact symptom reproduces only in the reverse order: an OBJECT write that makes a field readonly is never judged against the live flows that write it, because the rule's suite member keeps the default `flow` write type (`packages/lint/src/reference-integrity-suite.ts:756`, default at `:197`) and an object write's snapshot carries no `flows` collection (`RuntimeStackContext`, `packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts:326`; host gather, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts:412`). Closing that half means carrying live flows into the object write's snapshot. That changes the snapshot's documented contract (a context row is added only for a collection a rule resolves into) and the publish door's cost, and it would refuse an object publish because of a flow. That is a product and contract decision, so it is left to the seat (see Acceptance notes).

The fix line was the second half of the card: the rule's own remedy, `runAs: 'system'`, is the change that made the card's button answer 403.

## Tests

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/validate-readonly-flow-writes.test.ts src/rule-explanations.test.ts`: 2 files, 64 tests passed. The `[#32666]` describe pins the key clause (`'screen' or 'api' flow`, `subflow node`) on both verbs of an `autolaunched` flow, its absence on the four other flow types, and the `os explain` facts. Each fired line is held to one line of at most 200 characters by the existing `[#22161]` pin (longest new line: 189).
- Ablation, after committing the change: `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced `const buttonStarted = flow.type === BUTTON_STARTED_FLOW_TYPE;` with `const buttonStarted = false as boolean;` (anchor 1 → 0, blob `47e2252b` → `cf13212c`); the file went red, 3 failed and 53 passed, on exactly the three autolaunched cases; restored, blob back to `47e2252b` = HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty. The test imports the rule by relative path, so no `dist/` was involved.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/protocol-publish-drafts-closure.test.ts`: 1 file, 13 tests passed (4 new). These pin unchanged behaviour (they pass on `main` too), so there is no ablation for them.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test`: 199 files, 8544 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol typecheck`: exit 0; `--listFiles` shows both touched test files in a compiled program.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/migrations`: 5 files, 198 tests passed (no migration entry is added; run because the dispatch named it).

## Acceptance notes

- **Open, for the seat: the reverse order.** An object publish that makes `readonly: true` a field a live `runAs: 'user'` flow writes is accepted, and the flow then reports success while writing nothing. The options are in the os-dev report on the card. In short: (A) carry the package's live flows into an OBJECT write's snapshot only, and add `object` to this member's write types, so that object publish is refused (the finding sits on the flow and this write is charged with it, by the gate's existing differential); (B) the same input, reported as an advisory on the object write instead of a refusal; (C) leave the gate and make the run say so to the person who clicked. Both A and B add a `sys_metadata` read and a registry walk to every object publish.
- **Declarations.** The claim carried `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` for the narrowing the dispatch's mechanism assumed. This diff narrows nothing an author can write: the rule, its severity and what it refuses are unchanged, so the lines above say `no` and `none`. No ADR-0087 entry is registered, because there is no narrowing for one to describe. If the seat rules option A, that PR carries the claim's lines and the D3 entry. The seat's notice asked for the claim's lines and `Fixes`. They are not used here, for three reasons. `narrowed` with a `patch` changeset reds Check Changeset. A narrowing marker would need a D3 entry describing a refusal this diff does not add. And the reverse-order half the card reproduces stays open. The seat can edit the body if it rules otherwise.
- **Exposure** (the rule over every shipped stack, on this head): `examples/app-crm`, `app-multi-package` (its packages carry manifests only), `app-showcase`, `app-todo` and `packages/apps/connector-docusign`, `-github`, `-stripe`: 45 flows, 32 objects, 0 findings. `packages/apps/account`, `setup` and `studio` declare no flows. The same reading bounds option A's refusal exposure on the shipped corpus.
- **Out of scope, for the seat to card:** a flow step that dropped fields does not say so to the person who clicked. The engine logs the WARN (`packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts:2214`), and the step output carries `droppedFields` and `warnings` (`packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts:929`). But the trigger door's answer on the real kernel was `success: true`, with node `upd` at `status: success`, `acted: 1`, and no warning in the response. Seat disposition: carrier #32666 — this is option C of the open decision on that card (6824493421), so it is not carded separately.
- **Dogfood battery:** not run. The title has no `!` and `Clause-②` has no `(narrowing)` arm, which are the two triggers in the os-dev Definition of done.

## Verification

Gate readings come from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (the same 67 commands on both heads: 5 changed paths, against merge base `6bbdf301` before the merge and `d094752f` after it). Each exit code was captured before any pipe.

- **Merged head `fa9c0155`** (main merged in at `d094752f`): 66 of 67 run. `--ran` answers 67 derived, 66 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 1 UNRUN: `pnpm check:where-matcher` was not rerun here, on the seat's instruction to open the PR now, so it is NOT MEASURED on this head (it exited 0 on `b59783a3`). `pnpm check:dts-closure` exited 1 because `@object-ui/app-shell` had no `dist/index.d.ts`, left by a build of mine that timed out partway. After `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell build` it exited 0 (118 packages, 310/310 declaration files). After the merge: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test` passed (199 files, 8551 tests), the closure test passed 13/13, and both packages' typecheck exited 0.
- **Pre-merge head `b59783a3`**: 67 of 67 run, 65 exited 0 on the first pass. Two refused a prerequisite (exit 3), and both exited 0 when rerun on the same head: `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` after fetching its pinned commit `621a4876` (the clone was shallow), and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` after building the 7 packages that had no `dist/`. With those reruns recorded, `--ran` answers 67 derived, 67 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED.
- **CI-only families:** CI runs the whole farm. Its check-runs are read on the PR, not rerun here.
